home.lead: Cinematic brand films for beauty and health practices — dermatology, plastic surgery, medical aesthetics, cosmetic dentistry. Shot by me. Produced by my team at Divan Group.
home.entity: **Cinematic Clinic** is the film practice of **Shahab Balamchi**, a Toronto-based commercial cinematographer who has spent seven years inside beauty and health clinics — more than forty of them, over five thousand hours behind the lens. Every film is produced with his team at Divan Group and delivered in Canada, the United States, Spain and the UAE, in English and Persian.

offers.d: One shoot day. A 60–90 second cinematic brand film, six vertical cuts for social, twenty stills, full usage rights. For openings, rebrands, second locations and new treatments.
A profile film and ten short scripted episodes that make the doctor or owner the face of the practice — calm, credible, on camera.
I travel to one city for a week and film three to five clinics back to back — the United States, Spain and the UAE. Same eye, same standard, shared travel.

home.whyTitle: Why a person, not an agency

why.t: You are letting someone into a private room.
why.d: A clinic is a medical space where people are seen at their most vulnerable. Whoever holds the camera has to understand skin, consent and silence before they understand shutter speed. That is a person, with a name, who has done it forty times — not a rotating crew.

why.t: I do for myself what I sell to you.
why.d: The Doctor Series is founder-led content. I am my own first client: this site, these films and my own channels are built the same way I will build yours.

why.t: One filmmaker, a whole studio behind him.
why.d: I shoot every clinic film personally. Editing, colour, graphics, ads and the monthly content system are handled by my team at Divan Group — so the film does not end on delivery day.

home.processTitle: Concept to delivery, one hand on the camera

process.d: Thirty minutes on the clinic: what it does, what is changing, who should walk in after watching, and what it should feel like.
The space and light audit — rooms, windows, fluorescents, schedule — then a 40+ shot list and a consent plan for everyone on camera.
One calm day inside the clinic. Real practitioners, real rooms, patients only with written consent. Lit for skin, shot on cinema-grade cameras.
Edit, colour, licensed music. The brand film, the vertical cuts and the stills, delivered with full usage rights.

home.consentNote: Patients come first on every set. Read the [on-set consent & privacy protocol](/consent/) before we film.

faq.q: What is a clinic brand film?
faq.a: A 60–90 second cinematic film that shows how a clinic feels — the space, the practitioners, the care — rather than listing services. It lives on the website, the Google Business Profile, Instagram and in ads, and it is usually the first thing a new patient watches.

faq.q: How long does a shoot take?
faq.a: The Clinic Film is one shoot day. The Doctor Series is half a day. Pre-production happens before, in one conversation and one space audit, so the clinic keeps operating with minimal disruption.

faq.q: Do you film patients?
faq.a: Only with written consent, and never without the clinic's sign-off. Most brand films use staff, models and consenting patients. The full protocol is published on the consent page.

faq.q: Which countries do you work in?
faq.a: Canada, the United States, Spain and the UAE. Outside Canada I batch clinics into a Film Week — one city, three to five clinics, one trip — so the travel is shared.

faq.q: Do you work in Persian?
faq.a: Yes. I am fully bilingual in English and Persian, and many of the clinic owners I work with in Toronto, Dubai and Los Angeles prefer to plan in Persian and publish in English.

faq.q: What happens after the film?
faq.a: Most clinics continue with monthly content, ads and reporting through my team at Divan Group, the studio behind every Cinematic Clinic film. The film is the front door; the system keeps it open.

home.manifesto: Most clinic content delivers proof. **Proof no longer differentiates.** Clinics compete on perception, on trust, on how it feels to walk in. Cinematic Clinic turns a practice into a film — and the film into the reason a patient books.

selected.d: Rooms, light and pace, before a single treatment is named. The film that answers the question every new patient has: what is it like there?
The people behind the practice, on camera and at ease. Trust attaches to faces, not logos.
A walk through the clinic the way a first-time patient sees it — reception to treatment room.

clinicFilm.title: The Clinic Film — Cinematic Brand Film for Clinics
clinicFilm.metaDesc: A cinematic 60–90 second brand film for a beauty or health clinic: one shoot day, six vertical cuts, twenty stills, full usage rights.
clinicFilm.lead: One day inside your clinic. One film that shows what it feels like to be treated there — and a set of cuts that carry that feeling across every channel.
intro: **The Clinic Film** is a cinematic brand film for a single beauty or health practice: dermatology, plastic surgery, medical aesthetics, cosmetic dentistry, wellness. It is filmed by Shahab Balamchi in one shoot day and produced by Divan Group. Clinics commission it at five moments — an opening, a rebrand, a second location, a new device or treatment, and when the owner decides the practice needs a face.
No two clinics are scoped the same, so there is no price list. Send one message about the clinic and I will come back with a scope.

list: A **60–90 second brand film**, colour-graded, with licensed music, delivered in 16:9 and 9:16.
**Six vertical cuts** (15–30 seconds) for Instagram, TikTok and paid social — each one a complete idea, not a trailer.
**Twenty stills** from the shoot, retouched for web, Google Business Profile and print.
**Full usage rights** transferred to the clinic on delivery. No licence renewals, ever.
Signed **consent releases** for every person who appears on camera.

steps.d: What the clinic does, what is changing, who should walk in after watching, and what it should feel like.
Rooms, windows, fluorescents, reflections and the day's schedule. A 40+ shot list and a consent plan follow.
One calm day. Real practitioners and real rooms; patients only with written consent. Lit for skin.
Cut for feeling first, information second. Graded so skin looks like skin. Music licensed for the clinic's channels.
Master files, social cuts, stills and releases in one folder, with a short note on where each piece works best.

p: It is not monthly content, ads management or SEO. Those live with my team at Divan Group and most clinics add them after the film. It is not hourly videography either — a Clinic Film is scoped as a project with a fixed deliverable, because a clinic should know exactly what it is getting.

faq.q: How much disruption does a shoot day cause?
faq.a: Very little. I work around the schedule, room by room, and most clinics keep seeing patients. The audit before the shoot is what makes this possible.

faq.q: Who appears in the film?
faq.a: Practitioners and staff, and patients or models who have signed a release. I never film a patient without written consent and the clinic's sign-off.

faq.q: Can we use the film in ads?
faq.a: Yes. Full usage rights transfer to the clinic, including paid media, and the music is licensed accordingly.

faq.q: Do you film outside Toronto?
faq.a: Across Canada, and in the United States, Spain and the UAE through Film Week — batched shoots in one city so travel is shared between clinics.

faq.q: How do I get a quote?
faq.a: Send one message about the clinic from the contact page. I reply personally with a scope and a proposed shoot window.

doctorSeries.title: The Doctor Series — Video for Physicians & Owners
doctorSeries.metaDesc: A profile film and ten scripted short episodes that make the physician or clinic owner the face of the practice. Half a day on set.
doctorSeries.eyebrow: For the physician · The Doctor Series
doctorSeries.lead: People choose a doctor before they choose a clinic. This series puts the practitioner on camera — calm, credible and consistent — in a profile film and ten short episodes.
intro: **The Doctor Series** is a founder-led video series for a physician, surgeon, dentist or clinic owner. In half a day we film a 60-second profile piece and ten vertical episodes, each answering one question a patient actually asks. Scripts are prepared together beforehand; on the day, my job is to make the doctor forget the camera is there.
It is the same thing I do for myself. Trust in this industry attaches to people, not logos, and the practitioner who explains things clearly on camera becomes the one patients ask for by name.

list: A **60-second profile film** of the practitioner — who they are, what they believe about care.
**Ten vertical episodes** (30–60 seconds), each answering one patient question, ready for Instagram, TikTok, YouTube Shorts and the website.
**Scripting** from a question list built with the clinic, and a short **on-camera guide** sent before the shoot.
**Captions** in English, with Persian available, and full usage rights.

steps.d: We collect the twenty questions patients ask most, then choose ten. The answers are the doctor's, in their own words.
Two set-ups in the clinic, lit for skin, with a teleprompter available but rarely needed after the first take.
Cut tight, captioned, graded, delivered as one library the clinic can publish over three months.

p: A physician opening a practice, a surgeon joining a group, a dentist moving into aesthetics, an owner who wants the clinic to have a face — and any practitioner who has been told they should be on camera and has been putting it off.

faq.q: I am not comfortable on camera. Does this still work?
faq.a: That is the normal starting point. The scripts are the doctor's own answers, the set is quiet, and the first twenty minutes are for getting comfortable. Nobody watches those.

faq.q: Can the episodes be in Persian?
faq.a: Yes — in Persian, English or both. Captions follow the language of the episode.

faq.q: Can we combine it with the Clinic Film?
faq.a: Yes, and most clinics do: the Clinic Film sets the scene, the Doctor Series gives it a voice. Combined shoots are scoped as one project.

faq.q: How do we keep the momentum after ten episodes?
faq.a: Through monthly content with my team at Divan Group — the same question-led format, filmed on a regular cadence.

cta.text: Tell me who the series is for and what patients keep asking them.

filmWeek.title: Film Week — Clinic Brand Films in the US, Spain & UAE
filmWeek.metaDesc: Shahab Balamchi travels to one city for a week and films three to five clinics back to back, with shared travel and local crew.
filmWeek.lead: One city. One week. Three to five clinics filmed back to back, to the same standard as Toronto — with the travel shared and a local crew beside me.
intro: **Film Week** is how Cinematic Clinic works outside Canada. Instead of flying for a single clinic, I travel to one city — Los Angeles, Dubai, Barcelona — for five to seven days and film several clinics in a row. Each clinic receives a full Clinic Film or Doctor Series; the travel cost is shared, and a local second shooter from the Film Academy network supports the shoot and any follow-up.
A Film Week is confirmed when three clinics in the same city have signed. Dates are announced to the waitlist first.

list: **United States** — Los Angeles first, where the Persian-speaking clinic community is strongest; other cities on request.
**Spain** — Barcelona, with the Divan Group network on the ground.
**United Arab Emirates** — Dubai, in English, Persian and with Arabic-speaking practitioners on camera.
**Canada** — Toronto is home; Montreal and Vancouver are scheduled as regular trips.

steps.d: Tell me the city and the clinic. No commitment yet — this builds the list that decides the dates.
When three clinics in one city have signed, the week is booked and the schedule is shared.
The conversation and the space audit happen on video before I fly; consent plans and shot lists are ready on arrival.
One clinic per day, a local crew for logistics, and an extra day for weather, reshoots and stills.
Edit, colour and captions by the Divan Group team; delivery within the same window as any Toronto project.

p: Flying a filmmaker in for one clinic is expensive and, worse, rushed. Batching lets each clinic get a full, unhurried shoot day at a fraction of the travel cost, and it means the same eye films every clinic in the city — which is exactly what a group with several locations wants.

faq.q: What does a clinic pay for?
faq.a: Its own Clinic Film or Doctor Series, plus a shared portion of the travel at cost. No price list is published; every clinic receives a written scope.

faq.q: What if only two clinics sign?
faq.a: The week waits until a third confirms. Registered clinics hear first and are never charged for a trip that does not happen.

faq.q: Can a group book a whole week?
faq.a: Yes. A group with three or more locations in one city can book the week outright, and the schedule is built around them.

faq.q: Which languages?
faq.a: English and Persian by me directly; Arabic and Spanish through local crew and translated scripts.

academy.lead: A complete cinematography course for videographers who want to master the highest-paying niche in commercial film — taught by an operator who films clinics every week.
intro: Every week a videographer asks me the same question: *how do you make clinics look like that?* The honest answer is a method, not a camera. The **Film Academy for the Beauty Business** is that method — six modules covering everything from how to enter the niche to how to turn one shoot into a monthly retainer.

It is camera-agnostic (my own examples are shot on Sony A7R V and A7 III), subtitled in English and Persian, with Persian voice-over on selected modules. Cohort dates are announced to the waitlist first; waitlist members receive founder pricing, lifetime access and a private Q&A call.
academy.modulesTitle: Six modules. One craft. Taught honestly.

modules.d: Entry strategy, portfolio building, and clinic-specific legal and privacy rules.
Discovery scripts, space audits, and a 40+ shot template.
Camera settings, a three-lens kit, fluorescent management, gimbal technique — lit for skin.
Edit structures, colour grading, a custom LUT pack, music licensing.
Package pricing, contract clauses, consent releases, payment workflows.
Monthly retainer conversion, content calendars, productised offers.

academy.operatorTitle: Taught by an operator, not a guru
operator: I am Shahab Balamchi — a commercial cinematographer in Toronto and the founder of Divan Group. For seven years I have filmed the clinics, med spas and aesthetic practices that shape how the beauty business is seen: more than forty of them, over five thousand hours behind the lens, across Canada, the United States, Spain and the UAE.

The Academy teaches exactly what I do on set this week — nothing theoretical, nothing I have not sold. Graduates in other cities also become the local crew for Film Week, so the course is a door into real work, not just a certificate.
waitlist: Cohort dates, founder pricing and the private Q&A go to this list first. For videographers with two or more years of experience; clinic owners and marketing managers who want to brief creators better are welcome too.

faq.q: Who is the course for?
faq.a: Videographers with two or more years of experience who want to specialise in beauty and medical aesthetics. Clinic owners and marketing managers also take it to learn how to brief and judge video work.

faq.q: Do I need a specific camera?
faq.a: No. The method is camera-agnostic. My examples use Sony A7R V and A7 III, but the lighting, shot lists and edit structures apply to any mirrorless or cinema camera.

faq.q: Is it available in Persian?
faq.a: All modules have English and Persian subtitles, and selected modules have Persian voice-over.

faq.q: When does it start?
faq.a: Cohort dates are announced to the waitlist first. Join the list to hear the date and receive founder pricing.

faq.q: Is there a refund policy?
faq.a: Yes — a 14-day refund policy from the day of access.

about.title: About Shahab Balamchi — Clinic Filmmaker, Toronto
about.metaDesc: Shahab Balamchi has filmed 40+ beauty and health clinics over seven years and founded Divan Group. Toronto. English and Persian.
about.lead: Fifteen years behind the camera. Seven of them inside clinics.
about.statement: I’m Shahab Balamchi, a *clinic filmmaker*. For seven years I’ve filmed the beauty and health practices people trust with their faces — 40+ clinics across Canada, the United States, Spain and the UAE. I make the film that shows how your clinic *feels*. My team at Divan Group turns it into everything else.
bio: I started in videography and photography, founded **Divan Group** in Toronto in 2015, and somewhere around the fortieth clinic realised that filming medical and aesthetic practices had become its own craft — with its own light, its own rules about consent, and its own way of making a room feel safe on screen. **Cinematic Clinic** is that craft, under my own name.

I work in English and Persian, which matters more than it sounds: many of the clinic owners I film in Toronto, Dubai and Los Angeles plan in one language and publish in the other. I shoot on cinema-grade mirrorless cameras, light for skin rather than for rooms, and I would rather turn the fluorescents off and wait for the window than fake it.

consent.title: On-Set Patient Consent & Privacy Protocol
consent.metaDesc: How we film inside clinics: written consent for every person on camera, nothing without the clinic's sign-off, secure storage, deletion on request.
consent.lead: What we film, what we never film, and what happens to the footage. Published so that every clinic, practitioner and patient knows the rules before the camera is unpacked.
intro: A clinic is a medical space. Filming inside it is a privilege that depends on trust, so this protocol applies to every Cinematic Clinic and Divan Group shoot, in every country, without exception. Where a clinic's own regulator or privacy law is stricter, the stricter rule applies.

list: **Written consent** from every identifiable person on camera — practitioners, staff, models and patients — before filming, on a release form the clinic keeps a copy of.
**Patients are never filmed without the clinic's sign-off**, and never during a consultation or procedure unless that is explicitly what they have agreed to.
Consent can be **withdrawn** at any point before publication, in writing, and the footage is removed from the edit.
**Minors are not filmed** as patients. Minors appearing incidentally (for example, a family member in reception) are excluded from the frame or blurred.
Filming zones are agreed in the space audit; **no camera in any room that has not been cleared** for that time slot.
Signage at reception tells patients that filming is taking place and how to avoid it.
Screens, charts, whiteboards and paperwork with patient information are **turned, covered or removed** before a shot is set up.
Before-and-after material is filmed **only from the clinic's own consented records**, never captured new on set without a specific release.
Raw footage is stored on encrypted drives and in access-controlled cloud storage; it is never shared with third parties for any purpose other than producing the clinic's deliverables.
Raw material involving patients is **deleted on request** at any time and, by default, twelve months after final delivery.
The clinic receives full usage rights to the finished films and stills; Cinematic Clinic and Divan Group use finished work in their own portfolios **only with the clinic's written permission**.

p: Clinics remain responsible for compliance with their own professional and privacy rules — for example PHIPA in Ontario, HIPAA in the United States, the GDPR in Spain, and the UAE Personal Data Protection Law — and this protocol is designed to make that easy to demonstrate. Release templates are provided; a clinic may substitute its own.

consent.note: This protocol describes how we work; it is not legal advice. Version 1, September 2026. Questions: balamchi@divangroup.ca.

privacy.title: Privacy Notice | Cinematic Clinic
privacy.metaDesc: How cinematicclinic.com handles the information you send through its forms.
privacy.lead: Short, because we collect very little.

p: Only what you type into the contact or waitlist forms: your name, email, clinic or city, and your message. The site sets no advertising cookies and runs no tracking pixels. The film on the homepage plays automatically and muted from YouTube's privacy-enhanced domain; every other video loads only after you press play.

To reply to you. Form submissions are delivered by email to balamchi@divangroup.ca through a transactional email service and are not added to any marketing list. Waitlist members receive Academy announcements only, and can leave the list by replying to any email.
Ask at any time to see, correct or delete what we hold about you: balamchi@divangroup.ca. Cinematic Clinic is operated by Shahab Balamchi, Toronto, Canada, as a Divan Group production.
